Let <MATH_0001> be a locally Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is universally catenary,
<STRUCT_0003> there exists an open covering of <MATH_0003> all of whose members are
universally catenary schemes,
<STRUCT_0004> for every affine open <MATH_0004> the ring
<MATH_0005> is universally catenary, and
<STRUCT_0005> there exists an affine open covering <MATH_0006> such
that each <MATH_0007> is the spectrum of a universally catenary ring.
<STRUCT_0006>
Moreover, in this case any scheme locally of finite type over <MATH_0008>
is universally catenary as well.

By Lemma <REF_0001> an open immersion
is locally of finite type. A composition of morphisms locally of
finite type is locally of finite type
(Lemma <REF_0002>). Thus it is clear that if <MATH_0001> is
universally catenary then any open and any scheme locally of finite
type over <MATH_0002> is universally catenary as well. This proves the final
statement of the lemma and that (1) implies (2).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
If <MATH_0003> is a universally catenary scheme, then every
scheme <MATH_0004> with <MATH_0005> a finite type <MATH_0006>-algebra is
catenary. Hence all these rings <MATH_0007> are catenary by
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0003>.
Thus <MATH_0008> is universally catenary. Combined with the remarks above we
conclude that (1) implies (3), and (2) implies (4). Of course
(3) implies (4) trivially.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
To finish the proof we show that (4) implies (1).
Assume (4) and let <MATH_0009> be a morphism locally of finite type.
We can find an affine open covering <MATH_0010> such that
each <MATH_0011> maps into one of the <MATH_0012>. By
Lemma <REF_0004>
the induced ring map <MATH_0013> is
of finite type. Hence <MATH_0014> is catenary. Hence
<MATH_0015> is catenary by Properties, Lemma <REF_0005>.
